record.what_it_does: Notion is a workspace app for notes, docs, wikis, and databases, and its REST API lets external apps read, create, and update pages, databases, users, and comments in a workspace.
record.auth_notes: Notion has three connection types: internal connections (static 'installation access token', single workspace), public connections (OAuth 2.0, installable across workspaces, can be Marketplace-listed), and personal access tokens (user-scoped static bearer token, no OAuth flow). All three authenticate API requests with a Bearer token in the Authorization header. A multi-user agent toolkit would use the public connection OAuth2 flow so each end user can individually authorize and pick which pages/databases to share.
record.access_notes: Any developer can create an internal connection in the Developer portal and get a working API token immediately at no cost, or create a public (OAuth2) connection and use it without listing it on the Marketplace. Listing on the Notion Marketplace requires a Notion security review, but that review is only needed for public marketplace distribution, not for building or using the API.
record.main_blocker: Public (Marketplace) distribution requires Notion security review; official MCP server only supports user OAuth, not headless bearer-token auth

evidence.quote: Public connections use OAuth 2.0 for authentication. At creation time, you choose their installation scope
Personal access tokens (PATs) are created directly by a Notion user in the Developer portal. There is no OAuth flow
We recommend starting with an internal connection — it's the fastest way to begin building. You get an API token immediately
Public connections must undergo a Notion security review before being listed on the Marketplace. You can create and use a public connection without listing it.
The Notion API follows RESTful conventions when possible, with most operations performed via GET, POST, PATCH, and DELETE requests
Notion MCP (https://mcp.notion.com/mcp) is our hosted, actively maintained server. It uses OAuth for authentication
Notion MCP requires user-based OAuth authentication and does not support bearer token authentication
The body of the request contains a `verification_token`, which proves that Notion can successfully reach your endpoint.

record.open_questions: Exact rate limits and whether internal-connection tokens are subject to any Marketplace-style review were not checked; not expected to change buildability.
